notes: US 708 (also HVS 2 and SDSSJ093320.86+441705.4): the paper's final assessment retains it as the only hot-subdwarf HVS (T:p1-b6, T:p5-b5), so it is classified as candidates_found even though it is a previously known object. HVS 2 is grouped with US 708 because the historical passage connects the He-sdO HVS 2 discovery with the object subsequently identified as US 708 (T:p1-b8; Fig. 1 caption T:p2-b0). SDSSJ205030.39-061957.8 (J2050-063): explicitly named among the dozen earlier candidate HVS subdwarfs (T:p3-b1) and re-analysed here (T:p5-b0, T:p5-b3), but the final kinematics find the sample bound apart from US 708 (T:p5-b5, T:p7-b2), hence follow_up. The labels J0845 and J1459 in the Kiel diagram (I:p6-b0) mark individual plotted stars, but the paper does not explicitly identify either as a previously proposed Galactic-unbound candidate; labels alone do not establish candidacy. The unnamed binary sdB from Németh et al. (T:p3-b1) is likewise omitted because no identifier or explicit Galactic-unbound candidacy statement is supplied.

US 708: US 708 is the He-sdO also designated SDSSJ093320.86+441705.4 (HVS 2). The paper does not explicitly tabulate equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper-motion components, or numerical bound/unbound probabilities. The radial velocity is read approximately from the arrow labelled US 708 in Fig. 2. The paper additionally quotes an ejection velocity from the Galactic disk of 897 km/s, but this is not the Galactic rest-frame speed and is not extracted as such.

SDSSJ205030.39-061957.8: The target SDSSJ205030.39-061957.8 (J2050-063) is identified only as a He-sdO hyper-velocity-star candidate and “US708 twin” (T:p3-b1; T:p5-b3). Its spectrum is fitted in Fig. 4 (I:p5-b0), but no numerical astrometric, photometric, spectroscopic, distance, velocity, or probability values are reported specifically for this star. The statement that sample stars are bound to the Galaxy and belong to a halo population (T:p5-b5) is qualitative and not a per-star numerical value, so no quantities are retained.
